dedupe_keys.name: data center watch local opposition to us data centre projects

description: Data Center Watch tracks local opposition to data centre development in the United States. Its first report, covering May 2024 to March 2025, found that $18 billion of projects had been blocked by permit denials or developer withdrawals and $46 billion delayed, with at least 142 activist groups organising in 24 states against construction or expansion, and later quarterly briefings report that project disruption has stayed high and opposition has become more local and project specific, targeting permits, infrastructure and policy decisions. The research uses public sources, including local media, government filings, petitions, social media and official statements, and the underlying database is updated continuously. Commentators citing the tracker report that water use is the concern raised most often, in more than 40 per cent of contested projects, followed by energy demand and electricity prices, and that cancellations rose from 2 projects in 2023 to 25 in 2025. Coverage: the United States, 2024 onward. Format and access: PDF report and quarterly briefings, free; the project database itself is not published for download. Caveats: dollar values are estimates from announcements; counts depend on media coverage. Simulation uses: social acceptance constraints and delay probabilities in scenarios of data-centre build-out, and siting studies that weigh community impacts. Related records: dcmap.us and the IM3 atlas list the projects and sites, and the Virginia air permit data relate to one common local concern.
